description:

Guidehouse seeks a Data Analyst to support data analytics and visualization, program evaluation, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, and operational improvement engagements across federal civilian agencies. This role will help clients transform complex datasets into actionable insights that support strategic decision making, organizational design and staffing model development, workforce planning, and performance management.
As a Data Analyst, you will work with multidisciplinary consulting teams, subject matter experts, and client stakeholders to collect and structure complex datasets, perform quantitative and qualitative analyses, develop data visualizations and management tools to support data-driven decision making, construct models and algorithms to support forecasting efforts, and deliver data-driven recommendations for complex public sector challenges.

What You Will Do :

- Collaborate with team members and clients to collect, validate, structure, manage, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data to produce actionable insights that can drive client decision making.

- Conduct benchmarking and comparative analyses, research, and data collection activities to support organizational assessments, program evaluations, and workforce studies.

- Perform forecasting, trend analysis, and scenario modeling to support organizational design and staffing model development, workforce planning, and performance management efforts.

- Develop client-ready dashboards, visualizations, and analytical products that can support client executive oversight and operational decision making.

- Translate analytical findings into client-ready recommendations that can support strategic decision-making and organizational transformation.

- Support survey design, survey analysis, and qualitative research activities.

- Support the development of client-ready deliverables, including formal written reports, presentations, and executive-level briefings for client stakeholders.

- Facilitate client meetings and working sessions.

- Contribute to proposal development, thought leadership, and internal capability-building initiatives.

What You Will Need:

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.

- Must be a US Citizen due to nature of client engagements.

- Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Business, Engineering, Public Policy, or a related discipline.

- Three (3) to Five(5) years of professional experience, including 3+ years of experience performing quantitative analysis.

- Advanced Excel, data analysis, and visualization skills, including the ability to develop creative methods of joining multiple, disparate datasets to produce meaningful insights

- Demonstrated ability to develop visualizations and communicating analytical findings to non-technical audiences.

- Experience working with and structuring large and complex datasets to extract meaningful decision-ready insights.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to develop executive-level briefing materials.

What Would Be Nice To Have :

- Experience supporting federal civilian agencies.

- Experience with Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Python, R, Alteryx, or similar tools.

- Experience with forecasting, statistical analysis, or performance measurement.

- Experience supporting workforce studies, program evaluations, or organizational assessments.

- Experience presenting analytical findings to executive stakeholders.

- Master's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Business, Public Policy, Operations Research, or a related field.

The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team’s work supports developers, operators and sponsors to bring in new grid-scale and community renewables, storage and green fuels resources. The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team also assists utilities and large load companies in optimizing their long-term power supply strategies.
Our Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team develops and maintains a suite of quantitative market models that Guidehouse’s clients, renewable and storage players, and utilities depend on for capital investment decisions, business improvement and grid reliability. Through our wholesale and retail market expertise and modeling capabilities, we forecast energy market conditions across North America, along with generating resource additions and retirements, intra-day commercial optimization of assets using different market instruments, in an effort to identify business opportunities and quantify business risks. The Energy Markets & Systems Integrated Modeling Team maintains its independent view of North American wholesale power markets in its bi-annual Reference Case.

Responsibilities of a Senior Consultant include, but are not limited to, the following:

- Supporting large and complex client engagements.

- Tracking and analyzing energy market trends.

- Translating clients' inquiries and challenges into actionable scopes of work.

- Compiling reports, presentations, and other documents to communicate solutions, strategies, and analysis to clients.

- Developing and using analytical models, programming, and simulations to forecast market prices, conduct research and development, and create tools to improve productivity and accuracy.

- Reviewing and approving model outputs via data collection, manipulation, and analyses, which may involve spreadsheet and database creation and management.

On our team you’ll:

- Develop expertise in ISO/RTO markets across North America, at the crossroads of local energy pricing, capacity auctions, ancillary services and shifts in load composition and demand response initiatives

- Be intimately familiar with the economics, policies and players driving renewables, battery storage development, green fuels and new power generation technologies.

- Supervise simulations of the future dispatch of the power transmission grid using an economic dispatch model.

- Review the addition/retirement of diverse generating resources using a capacity expansion model across ISO/RTO markets.

- Understand how energy players procure power, integrate renewables, and maintain grid reliability.

- Help develop our Reference Case while expanding our client base.

title: Cloud and Health AI FinOps and Technology Value Optimization
description:
Job Family :
Technology Consulting
Travel Required :
Up to 50%
Clearance Required :
None

We are seeking a senior leader to build and lead our Cloud and AI FinOps and Technology Value Optimization capability for healthcare provider clients. This is a portfolio role, not a single-engagement role. The successful candidate will carry concurrent delivery accountability across multiple health system clients, own the commercial performance of that portfolio, shape the methodologies and assets that make the capability repeatable, and serve as the practice's most credible voice with CFOs, CIOs, and Chief Data and AI Officers on what cloud and AI actually cost and what value they actually return.
The immediate anchor assignment is a large academic medical center's Azure migration, where this leader will own a two-workstream program spanning cloud FinOps enablement and organizational change management. That engagement is the entry point to a broader agenda: as health systems move workloads and stand up AI platforms, they are discovering that consumption-based economics, fragmented application portfolios, and immature governance compound each other. This leader will connect those problems — FinOps discipline, application and AI workload rationalization, cloud operating model design, and the change management required to make any of it stick — into a coherent point of view and a growing book of work.
This role suits someone who is equally comfortable in front of a finance committee defending a commitment strategy, in a working session with cloud engineers debating tagging enforcement, and in a practice leadership meeting arguing for where to invest next. It carries real autonomy, real revenue accountability, and a clear path to Partner-track responsibility.

What You Will Do:
Client and Portfolio Leadership

- Hold delivery and commercial accountability for a portfolio of concurrent cloud and AI FinOps, rationalization, and technology value optimization engagements, including scope, quality, margin, staffing, risk posture, and client satisfaction across all of them.

- Serve as the senior client-facing voice with CFOs, CIOs, Chief Data and AI Officers, and their governance committees — framing tradeoffs, defending recommendations under scrutiny, and converting analysis into decisions leadership is willing to fund and act on.

- Set the standard for executive deliverables across the portfolio, personally shaping the narrative, structure, and defensibility of board- and committee-level materials rather than reviewing them at the margin.

- Manage the balance between advisory posture and hands-on execution, deploying the team into direct build work where client capacity is constrained without allowing the engagement to drift into unpriced staff augmentation.

Cloud and AI FinOps

- Lead establishment of durable FinOps capabilities for cloud and AI workloads, spanning consumption baselining, cost allocation and unit economics, showback and chargeback design, forecasting, anomaly management, and value realization tracking.

- Advise clients on enterprise agreement and commitment strategy, including commitment sizing and right-sizing, reservation and savings plan portfolios, consumption trajectory risk, and the financial exposure created by aggressive multi-year commitments.

- Bring a defensible point of view on AI and analytics workload economics — GPU and inference cost behavior, consumption-based data platform pricing, model and token-level attribution, and the shared-service allocation problems that make AI spend uniquely difficult to govern.

- Direct design of cloud operating model components that sustain FinOps beyond the engagement: Cloud Center of Excellence structures, intake and provisioning workflows, tagging taxonomies and enforcement automation, decision rights, policy guardrails, and recurring cost review routines.

- Oversee automation and reporting build-out across native cloud cost management tooling, data platform usage telemetry, and enterprise BI, ensuring clients inherit working instrumentation rather than a static assessment.

Cloud and AI Rationalization and Value Optimization

- Lead application and workload rationalization engagements, including portfolio inventory and segmentation, disposition analysis, cloud candidacy and workload placement criteria, migration wave sequencing, and the business cases that justify retire, consolidate, replatform, or modernize decisions.

- Extend rationalization discipline to the emerging AI estate — redundant models, pilots, copilots, and point solutions — and help clients distinguish AI investments that are compounding value from those that are accumulating cost and risk.

- Connect rationalization findings to run-rate reduction, contract and licensing optimization, technical debt retirement, and reinvestment capacity, quantified in terms finance leadership will stand behind.

- Partner with enterprise architecture, infrastructure, security, and data leaders to ensure disposition and placement recommendations account for interoperability, regulatory, data retention, and risk constraints specific to healthcare.

Change Enablement and Adoption

- Hold accountability for the organizational change management workstreams attached to cloud and AI programs, directing change strategy, stakeholder and impact assessment, communications, change networks, role-based training, and adoption measurement through dedicated change leads.

- Ensure the operating model and cost governance work is matched by genuine organizational adoption, treating readiness and behavior change as delivery outcomes rather than supporting activities.

Practice Building and Growth

- Originate and close follow-on and net-new work across the portfolio, including scoping, pricing, proposal development, and oral presentations, with accountability for an annual sales or expansion target.

- Build the reusable methodologies, accelerators, maturity models, benchmarks, and pricing constructs that turn repeated engagement work into a scalable practice capability.

- Represent the firm externally through thought leadership, conference participation, client roundtables, and hyperscaler and platform partner relationships that generate pipeline.

- Recruit, develop, and performance-manage consultants through senior manager level across FinOps, cloud engineering, application portfolio, and change management skill sets, and serve as career advisor to a group of professionals.

What You Will Need:

- Minimum of SEVEN (7)+ years of overall work experience.

- Bachelors degree from an accredited university.

- Experience in technology consulting, cloud and technology financial management, or technology transformation.

- Experience in engagement leadership level with accountability for delivery outcomes and commercial performance.

- Demonstrated ownership of a portfolio of concurrent engagements — not sequential single-project leadership — including staffing across teams, margin management, and executive relationship ownership at multiple accounts simultaneously.

- Deep command of cloud economics on at least one major hyperscaler, with Microsoft Azure strongly preferred, including enterprise agreements and commitment constructs, native cost management tooling, reservations and savings plans, tagging and policy enforcement, and allocation across shared and dedicated services.

- Track record establishing FinOps capabilities aligned to recognized frameworks across the inform, optimize, and operate domains, with evidence of capabilities that persisted after the consulting team departed.

- Substantive experience in application portfolio rationalization, workload placement, or technology cost reduction, including disposition frameworks, business case development, and executive decision governance.

- Working fluency in AI and data platform economics, including consumption-based analytics platforms, GPU and inference cost drivers, and the attribution challenges created by shared AI and analytics services.

- Demonstrated accountability for organizational change management as an integrated workstream, including change strategy, adoption measurement, and executive-level stakeholder management.

- Proven ability to sell — origination, scoping, pricing, proposal leadership, and closing — with a credible record of revenue generated or expanded.

- Executive presence sufficient to hold a room of C-suite healthcare leaders, including the judgment to deliver unwelcome findings about cost exposure, failed governance, or unrealistic business cases without losing the relationship.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

- Experience serving academic medical centers, integrated delivery networks, and other healthcare provider organizations, including fluency with service line economics, fund and grant accounting, research computing, and public institution procurement and governance constraints.

- Familiarity with the healthcare platforms that drive the majority of cloud and AI consumption, including Epic and Oracle Health ecosystems, enterprise data platforms, imaging, and clinical and research analytics workloads.

- FinOps Certified Professional credentials, Prosci or equivalent change management certification, and Azure architecture certifications; familiarity with the Cloud Adoption Framework and Well-Architected Framework.

- Experience building a consulting capability or offering from an early stage to a repeatable, multi-client business, including methodology development, pricing strategy, and team build-out.

- Established relationships with hyperscaler and platform partner field organizations that translate into co-sell pipeline.

- Experience with adjacent scopes that extend cloud FinOps engagements, including multi-cloud and SaaS spend management, sustainability and carbon reporting, and enterprise technology business management.

- Advanced degree such as an MBA, MHA, or master's in information systems, and a record of published thought leadership or conference speaking in cloud economics, AI governance, or healthcare technology strategy.

- US Citizenship is contractually required.

About the Role:
Healthcare organizations are committing to cloud and AI at a pace that has outrun their ability to govern the spend or prove the return. Commitments are signed before consumption is understood, workloads migrate before portfolios are rationalized, and AI pilots multiply faster than anyone can measure what they cost. The leader in this role will be the person clients call when they need that situation made legible and then fixed — and will build the team, methods, and market position that let the firm answer that call at scale. Success looks like clients who can defend every dollar of cloud and AI spend, portfolios that are meaningfully smaller and better governed, and a practice capability that outlasts any single engagement.

Job Description Summary
The Business/Systems Analyst will support requirements analysis, process definition, stakeholder engagement, and solution alignment for a large-scale agile software development and platform modernization program supporting the GrantSolutions contract. This role is responsible for eliciting, documenting, analyzing, and validating business needs, system requirements, workflows, data exchanges, integration dependencies, and operational impacts across multiple workstreams and Scrum teams. The Business/Systems Analyst will work closely with Product Owners, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, enterprise architects, vendors, Federal stakeholders, and end users to translate modernization objectives into clear, actionable requirements and support high-quality outcomes across the system development lifecycle.

What You Will Do :
We are seeking a strong Business/Systems Analyst to support requirements, process, and solution analysis for a large-scale GrantSolutions platform modernization effort. This role will work across business stakeholders, Federal users, vendors, architects, and agile delivery teams to define current-state and future-state workflows, clarify business needs, document functional and non-functional requirements, and support incremental capability delivery while maintaining continuity of the legacy system throughout the transition.
The Business/Systems Analyst will help bridge business operations, user needs, system functionality, data exchanges, and technical delivery in an iterative modernization environment. This individual will analyze and document requirements for a modern integration layer that enables new vendor-delivered capabilities to interface with legacy components as the modernized platform is built out over time. The role requires strong analytical judgment and collaboration with Product Owners, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, enterprise architects, vendors, executive leadership, and Federal stakeholders to support alignment with platform architecture, governance standards, release readiness, and program objectives.

- Elicit, analyze, document, and validate business, functional, non-functional, data, reporting, workflow, and integration requirements for a large-scale platform modernization program delivered through iterative agile execution.

- Develop current-state and future-state process flows, business rules, user stories, acceptance criteria, use cases, interface requirements, and operational impact analyses to support incremental modernization.

- Support modernization workstreams across the application development lifecycle, including integration-layer delivery, legacy coexistence, testing, deployment, training, and rollout activities.

- Collaborate with Product Owners, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, enterprise architects, vendors, and Federal stakeholders to refine backlogs, clarify scope, manage requirements traceability, and support prioritization of incremental capabilities.

- Analyze integration-related needs, including APIs, data exchange patterns, interface dependencies, shared services, system handoffs, and interactions between legacy components and modernized capabilities.

- Identify and document legacy coexistence considerations, including workflow continuity, system-of-record decisions, duplicate processing paths, data synchronization, testing scenarios, operational readiness, and transition impacts.

- Support requirements reviews, design discussions, sprint planning, backlog grooming, demonstrations, user acceptance testing, defect triage, change impact assessments, and release readiness activities.

- Maintain analysis artifacts, including requirements documentation, process flows, user stories, acceptance criteria, traceability matrices, decision logs, interface coordination materials, and stakeholder communications.

- Translate technical integration concepts, modernization constraints, and delivery dependencies into clear business language for technical and non-technical audiences.

- Foster strong working relationships across Federal stakeholders, vendors, delivery teams, architects, and partners to support coordinated modernization outcomes and long-term platform success.

What You Will Need :

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DoD "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred

- Bachelor’s degree required.

- Minimum of SIX (6) to EIGHT (8) years of experience performing business analysis, systems analysis, requirements management, process analysis, technology delivery support, agile delivery support, or related IT modernization work.

- Experience supporting platform modernization, system integration, or phased technology delivery efforts, including delivery of new capabilities while legacy systems remain operational.

- Working understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), platform modernization concepts, and incremental transition from legacy architecture to modular, API-enabled, cloud-aligned capabilities.

- Demonstrated ability to facilitate stakeholder discussions, ask probing questions, synthesize input, and build shared understanding across business, technical, and operational audiences.

- Knowledge of Agile and other delivery methodologies, with experience supporting iterative delivery across vendors, delivery teams, or governance forums.

- Strong experience applying business and systems analysis disciplines, including requirements elicitation, process mapping, user story development, acceptance criteria definition, stakeholder coordination, meeting facilitation, documentation, traceability, and change impact analysis.

- Exposure to integration-layer delivery, including APIs, data exchange patterns, interface dependencies, shared services, or handoffs between legacy and modernized capabilities.

- Ability to analyze vendor-delivered capabilities within a common platform architecture and support alignment to shared standards, release readiness criteria, requirements traceability, and governance decisions.

- Ability to identify, track, and escalate legacy coexistence risks, including workflow continuity, data synchronization, testing scope, release sequencing, and operational transition planning.

- Ability to translate technical integration concepts into clear requirements, process flows, user stories, acceptance criteria, risk summaries, decision logs, and stakeholder communications for both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Ability to proactively identify, document, escalate, and support resolution of requirements gaps, process conflicts, data issues, testing blockers, and stakeholder decisions in highly regulated, multi-stakeholder environments.

- Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills with a team-first mindset and solution-oriented approach.

- Demonstrates a continuous improvement mindset - seeks to understand before optimizing processes, relationships, and outcomes.

- Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage stakeholders at all levels in both written and verbal formats.

- Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to support alignment between delivery activities, technology roadmaps, platform architecture standards, and modernization priorities.

- Experience with business process, workflow automation, interoperability, and shared service initiatives that improve reuse, reduce duplication, and support incremental capability expansion.

title: AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer
description:
Job Family :
Software Development & Support
Travel Required :
None
Clearance Required :
Ability to Obtain Public Trust

AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer
We are seeking an AWS Lakehouse Data Engineer to design, implement, and operate the cloud-native data platform that powers AI/ML, analytics, reporting, and data visualization. You will build a modern lakehouse on Amazon S3 using AWS-native services and open table formats, providing Databricks-like capabilities while maintaining portability, strong governance, cost efficiency, and operational control. You will also develop scalable batch and streaming ingestion, Python and PySpark ETL/ELT pipelines, metadata and governance services, and automated cloud provisioning and CI/CD across environments.
This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys platform building, automation, performance optimization, and enabling advanced analytics through trusted, secure, and well-governed data.

What You Will Do

Build and Operate Data Pipelines (Batch and Streaming)

- Design and implement batch and streaming ingestion from APIs, relational databases, file drops, event streams, and external partners.

- Implement, test, and optimize ETL/ELT pipelines using Python and PySpark to produce curated, analytics-ready datasets for reporting, visualization, and machine learning.

- Implement incremental processing, change data capture (CDC), data contracts, schema validation, and reusable transformation frameworks.

- Improve pipeline reliability through automated testing, orchestration, monitoring, retry handling, and operational runbooks.

Deliver an AWS-Native Lakehouse Data Platform

- Design and implement a Delta Lakehouse-style data platform using AWS-native services to provide Databricks-like capabilities for data engineering, analysis, and data visualization.

- Build and manage a scalable lakehouse on Amazon S3 using Apache Iceberg and open columnar formats such as Apache Parquet.

- Implement SQL-like table reliability for data stored in Amazon S3, including ACID transactions, schema evolution, partition evolution, snapshot isolation, time travel, and rollback capabilities using Apache Iceberg.

- Enable fast, interactive querying of lakehouse data using AWS-native query and compute services such as Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Redshift where appropriate.

- Optimize performance and cost through partitioning, compaction, file sizing, statistics, caching, lifecycle policies, and efficient separation of compute and storage.

- Establish standardized development, test, and production environments with consistent configuration and controlled promotion across stages.

Metadata, Governance, Access Control, Lineage, and Quality

- Implement data governance and fine-grained access control using AWS-native services, including AWS Lake Formation, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), AWS Key Management Service (KMS), and related security services.

- Implement a managed metadata repository for dataset cataloging, ownership, business definitions, tagging, classification, and discoverability.

- Enable end-to-end lineage from source through transformation and consumption to support auditability, impact analysis, and regulatory requirements.

- Apply policy-based access, least-privilege permissions, row-, column-, and cell-level controls where required, data classification, retention, encryption, and secure data handling.

- Build operational data quality checks for freshness, completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, and anomaly detection, and publish measurable SLAs/SLOs.

AWS Automation, CI/CD, and Operations

- Implement automated AWS provisioning using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to create consistent environments and secure-by-default baselines.

- Build and enhance CI/CD for data pipelines and lakehouse components, including automated tests, security checks, validation gates, packaging, deployment, promotion, and rollback strategies.

- Implement observability with centralized metrics, logs, traces, alerts, dashboards, runbooks, and incident-response procedures.

- Continuously evaluate platform performance, scalability, reliability, security, and cost, and implement measurable improvements.

Cross-Team Collaboration and Documentation

- Work closely with data, application, analytics, AI/ML, security, networking, and cloud platform teams to support mission needs and delivery timelines.

- Maintain high-quality engineering documentation, including architecture diagrams, data models, SOPs, interface specifications, operational runbooks, and secure configuration baselines.

- Present technical findings, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What You Will Need

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related field, or FOUR (4) years equivalent practical experience in leu of degree.

- SIX (6) years of relevant experience.

- Hands-on experience implementing AWS-native data lake or lakehouse architectures using Amazon S3 and services such as AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Lake Formation, and Amazon Redshift.

- Strong experience developing production ETL/ELT pipelines using Python and PySpark, including data modeling, transformation, testing, performance tuning, and error handling.

- Hands-on experience with Apache Iceberg, including ACID transactions, snapshots, schema and partition evolution, time travel, table maintenance, and query optimization.

- Advanced SQL skills and experience supporting analytical queries, semantic layers, reporting tools, and data visualization workloads.

- Experience implementing metadata management and governance capabilities, including cataloging, lineage, ownership, classification, policy enforcement, and fine-grained access controls.

- Experience with AWS security fundamentals, including IAM and least privilege, KMS encryption, secrets management, network security, logging, and secure SDLC practices.

- Experience provisioning AWS resources using IaC and operating data platforms across multiple environments.

- Experience building or operating CI/CD pipelines for data workflows, including testing, packaging, deployment automation, environment promotion, and rollback.

- Ability to troubleshoot distributed data-processing workloads and optimize performance, reliability, and cost.

What Would Be Nice to Have

- Hands-on experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, or migrating Databricks workloads to AWS-native services and Apache Iceberg.

- Experience with AWS Step Functions, Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA), Amazon Kinesis, AWS Database Migration Service (DMS), AWS Lambda, Amazon MSK, or similar ingestion and orchestration services.

- Experience with modern DevOps practices and tools such as Git, Terraform, AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK, Jenkins, AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions, and Docker.

- Experience integrating lakehouse data with business intelligence and visualization tools such as Amazon QuickSight, Tableau, or Power BI.

- Experience using AI-assisted coding tools, such as GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor, or Kiro, to accelerate implementation while maintaining code quality, testing, review, privacy, and security controls.

- Knowledge graph and Graph RAG experience, including graph modeling, ontology and taxonomy alignment, entity resolution, relationship extraction, and hybrid retrieval that combines graph traversal with semantic or vector search.

The AI Lead will set the technical direction and lead the delivery of secure, scalable, and responsible artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions in federal and other highly regulated environments. The AI Lead will guide multidisciplinary teams, establish AI engineering and governance standards, and ensure solutions are reliable, auditable, cost-effective, and aligned with organizational priorities, security requirements, and responsible AI practices.

What You Will Do
·        Define the AI strategy, technical roadmap, reference architectures, and engineering standards that connect mission and business priorities to measurable outcomes.
·        Lead the end-to-end design and delivery of AI/ML and generative AI solutions, including data ingestion, model selection and development, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic workflows, deployment, monitoring, and sustainment.

The Business Analyst / Product Owner will combine deep business and systems analysis with product ownership to guide delivery for a large-scale agile software development and platform modernization program supporting the GrantSolutions contract. This role will define product outcomes, represent stakeholder and user needs, own and prioritize the product backlog, and translate business objectives into clear, testable requirements and incremental capabilities. The individual will partner with Federal stakeholders, end users, Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, enterprise architects, vendors, and delivery teams to maximize value, manage scope and dependencies, and support high-quality outcomes across the product lifecycle.

What You Will Do:
We are seeking a strong Business Analyst / Product Owner to lead product discovery, requirements analysis, backlog management, and value-based delivery for a large-scale GrantSolutions platform modernization effort. This role will serve as the primary bridge between Federal users, business stakeholders, vendors, architects, and agile delivery teams—establishing a clear product direction, defining current-state and future-state workflows, and ensuring that each release addresses validated user and program needs while maintaining continuity of the legacy system throughout the transition.
The Business Analyst / Product Owner will balance strategic product accountability with detailed analysis. This individual will shape the product vision and roadmap, make day-to-day priority and scope decisions within delegated authority, and maintain a ready, ordered backlog supported by clear user stories and acceptance criteria. The role will also analyze business processes, system functionality, data exchanges, integration dependencies, and operational impacts for a modern integration layer that enables vendor-delivered capabilities to coexist with legacy components. Strong judgment, facilitation, and communication are required to align delivery with platform architecture, governance standards, release readiness, measurable outcomes, and program objectives.

- Define and communicate the product vision, goals, roadmap, and measurable outcomes in alignment with Federal stakeholder priorities, user needs, modernization objectives, and platform strategy.

- Own, order, and continuously refine the product backlog; prioritize features, enablers, defects, and technical work based on business value, user impact, risk, dependencies, compliance needs, and delivery capacity.

- Elicit, analyze, document, and validate business, functional, non-functional, data, reporting, workflow, and integration requirements for iterative delivery.

- Translate business and user needs into product features, epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, process flows, business rules, use cases, interface requirements, and operational impact analyses.

- Serve as the day-to-day product decision-maker within delegated authority, clarifying scope, resolving requirement questions, negotiating tradeoffs, and escalating decisions that affect product strategy, funding, policy, or governance.

- Lead product discovery, backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, demonstrations, and release-planning activities; ensure work is sufficiently defined, prioritized, and ready for delivery.

- Review completed work against acceptance criteria, coordinate stakeholder validation, support user acceptance testing, and recommend acceptance or follow-up actions based on business outcomes and quality expectations.

- Analyze APIs, data exchange patterns, interface dependencies, shared services, system handoffs, and interactions between legacy components and modernized capabilities.

- Identify and manage legacy coexistence considerations, including workflow continuity, system-of-record decisions, duplicate processing paths, data synchronization, testing scenarios, release sequencing, operational readiness, and transition impacts.

- Partner with Scrum Masters, Technical Leads, architects, vendors, and Federal stakeholders to manage cross-team dependencies, align solution approaches, resolve delivery blockers, and coordinate incremental capability releases.

- Track product and delivery measures, gather user feedback, evaluate adoption and outcomes, and use evidence to adjust priorities and drive continuous improvement.

- Maintain product and analysis artifacts, including roadmaps, backlogs, requirements, process flows, traceability matrices, decision logs, release materials, interface coordination documentation, and stakeholder communications.

- Experience supporting platform modernization, system integration, or phased technology delivery efforts, including delivery of new capabilities while legacy systems remain operational.

- Working understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), platform modernization concepts, and incremental transition from legacy architecture to modular, API-enabled, cloud-aligned capabilities.

- Strong knowledge of Agile product delivery, including product discovery, outcome definition, roadmap planning, backlog ordering, refinement, sprint planning, acceptance, release planning, and continuous improvement across multi-team or multi-vendor environments.

- Demonstrated experience owning and prioritizing a product backlog, writing and refining epics and user stories, defining acceptance criteria, facilitating stakeholder decisions, and balancing user value, program priorities, risk, technical constraints, and team capacity.

- Exposure to integration-layer delivery, including APIs, data exchange patterns, interface dependencies, shared services, or handoffs between legacy and modernized capabilities.

- Ability to analyze vendor-delivered capabilities within a common platform architecture and support alignment to shared standards, release readiness criteria, requirements traceability, and governance decisions.

- Ability to identify, track, and escalate legacy coexistence risks, including workflow continuity, data synchronization, testing scope, release sequencing, and operational transition planning.

- Ability to translate technical integration concepts into clear requirements, process flows, user stories, acceptance criteria, risk summaries, decision logs, and stakeholder communications for both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Ability to proactively identify, document, escalate, and support resolution of requirements gaps, process conflicts, data issues, testing blockers, and stakeholder decisions in highly regulated, multi-stakeholder environments.

- Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage stakeholders at all levels in both written and verbal formats.

- Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to support alignment between delivery activities, technology roadmaps, platform architecture standards, and modernization priorities.

- Experience with business process, workflow automation, interoperability, and shared service initiatives that improve reuse, reduce duplication, and support incremental capability expansion.

- Embed security early and continuously across the software delivery lifecycle through automated static analysis, dependency scanning, container/image scanning, infrastructure scanning, configuration validation, and compliance evidence generation.

- Implement and support observability practices, including centralized logging, metrics, dashboards, alerts, tracing, operational health checks, and production readiness monitoring across modernized and legacy-integrated capabilities.

- Support secure environment management, including configuration management, access control, network segmentation, encryption, secrets handling, backup considerations, disaster recovery support, and change/release coordination.

- Minimum of FIVE (5) years of experience in platform engineering, DevSecOps, cloud engineering, infrastructure automation, site reliability engineering, systems engineering, or related technical roles.

- Hands-on experience with AWS services including ECS/EKS, Lambda, API Gateway, EventBridge, S3, RDS, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, IAM, and Systems Manager.

title: QA Database Administrator
description:
Job Family :
Database Administration
Travel Required :
Up to 10%
Clearance Required :
Ability to Obtain Public Trust

Our federal client conducts product testing, quality evaluations, and risk assessments to support market interventions and ensure pharmaceutical manufacturing quality. The associated data repository serves as a critical system of record underpinning regulatory decision-making for pharmaceutical products.
This role supports an internal audit of drug quality sampling and testing databases to ensure data integrity, regulatory compliance, and methodological consistency. The DBA will assess data quality, validate adherence to FDA standards, information management compliance and provide actionable recommendations to strengthen regulatory decision-making processes.

What You Will Do:

- Perform comprehensive reviews of database records and database maintenance to evaluate completeness, accuracy, and consistency in coordination with Quality Assurance Data Auditor Lead.

- Analyze variations in sampling and testing data ingestion\export pathways and assess impacts to data quality and integrity across data sources and systems.

- Verify data traceability from sample collection through final testing results.

- Utilize ETL tools and data queries to identify duplicate or missing entries along with any data anomalies.

- Assess completeness of analytical method documentation (e.g., review analyst worksheets and supporting documentation) and data to determine data gaps or data integration errors.

- Assess compliance of documentation and data controls with FDA regulations, guidance, information security (e.g. ATO, FISMA) and standard operating procedures.

- Evaluate completeness, and consistency and gaps in supporting documentation associated with testing activities and system documentation.

- Identify deviation, inconsistencies from established processes and risks impacting regulatory decisions.

- Conduct comprehensive data quality assessment to detect trends, data anatomies and performance variations in procedures and their potential impact on data quality.

- Generate assessment records, gap analysis and final assessment and improvements report under the guidance of the QA Data Auditor Lead and Client Program Manager.

What You Will Need:

- Bachelor’s Degree, r elevant experience may be substituted for formal education.

- Minimum five (5) years of relevant experience in federal information systems management, data management and database administration.

- Demonstrated ability to define data integration problems and analyze complex systems within regulatory or scientific domains.

- Experience developing analysis plans, evaluating data quality, and information security compliance.

- Strong knowledge of FDA regulations, data integrity principles (e.g., ALCOA+), and regulatory documentation standards.

- Ability to assess system specifications and recommend improvements for implementation.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including status reports, technical reports and audit documentation.

- Strong critical thinking and problem-solving capabilities in complex regulatory environments.

- Hybrid role requiring the ability to work onsite at the client location in Silver Spring, MD.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

- Certifications in database administration (e.g. Oracle\Microsoft DBA, RDMS), data management (I.e. CDMP-DAMA), Data Governance (e.g. DGSP or DCAM) or Data Quality (i.e. CDQP).

- Experience supporting regulatory quality surveillance initiatives, data systems and data management practices.

- Experience conducting internal audits or supporting regulatory inspections (e.g., FDA, ISO, GLP).

- Knowledge of database systems used for laboratory data management (e.g., LIMS), scientific instruments and laboratory equipment.

- Experience with data governance, quality frameworks, and process improvement methodologies.

- Experience translating audit findings into operational and system-level improvements.

- Exposure to advanced analytics tools to conduct research, evaluate data integrity and trends.

What You Will Do
The AI/Data Senior Consultant leads discrete workstreams and delivers advanced AI and data solutions. This role combines technical depth, client engagement, and mentorship of junior team members while driving real‑world AI adoption.

Key Responsibilities

- Design and implement scalable AI and data solutions from requirements to deployment

- Develop, test, and tune fraud prevention and detection rules in a variety of programming languages

- Develop and optimize machine learning models and analytics workflows

- Lead data analytics efforts in detecting fraud, waste, abuse, and improper payments and identifying key areas to target for program/payment integrity improvements

- Partner with clients to identify AI use cases and translate business needs into solutions

- Own client deliverables and contribute to executive‑level presentations

- Mentor C2 consultants and review technical work

- Ensure solutions align with governance, security, and responsible AI standards (as applicable)

What You Will Need:

- Must be able to OBTAIN and MAINTAIN a Federal or DHS "PUBLIC TRUST"; candidates must obtain approved adjudication of their PUBLIC TRUST prior to onboarding with Guidehouse. Candidates with an ACTIVE PUBLIC TRUST or SUITABILITY are preferred.

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college/university

- FIVE (5) or more years of experience in AI, data science, analytics, or engineering

- THREE (3) or more years of experience in a fraud/payment integrity-related role

- Strong development expertise in Python/R, SQL , and data modeling

- Strong statistical and data analytics expertise

- Proficiency working with various data structure formats (CSV/TXT, JSON, XML, Parquet, etc.)

- Experience developing, testing, and validating machine learning and other AI models at scale

- Experience with data visualization tools (PowerBI, Tableau, Looker, etc.)

- Experience with applying data analytics and artificial intelligence in the financial crime compliance and/or fraud, waste, and abuse prevention space

- Travel will be 25-50% for candidates not located in the DMV or NYC area

​
What Would Be Nice to Have:

- Experience building fraud and/or fincrime monitoring rules in one or more programming languages

- Proven ability to communicate complex concepts to non‑technical audiences

- Experience working for or supporting healthcare technology, healthcare business or healthcare process initiatives

- Cloud experience (AWS, Azure, GCP) including data and ML services

- Experience deploying models into production (MLOps)

- Experience with AI platforms (Databricks, Palantir, Vertex AI, SageMaker)

- Prior consulting or client‑facing delivery experience

- Federal or State Medicaid experience (directly as an employee or in a consulting role), particularly experience with fraud prevention and detection and/or program integrity experience with Medicaid
